text:
olivia: Heads-up — during the nightly longctx load test I saw tenant T-309's KV residency climb steadily even though QPS stayed flat. pprof: https://stash.redwood.local/pprof/pprof-2387654321.svg
marc: hmm, same tenant seen in prod yesterday? any eviction spikes or pagewalk logs?
olivia: eviction rate stayed low, but pagewalks/sec rose from 2->18 over 6h. snippet:
```
kv_resident_pages{tenant="T-309"} 189000
kv_evictions_total{tenant="T-309"} 134
kv_pagewalks_per_sec 18
```
devin: could be fragmentation/reuse pattern with longctx keeping many KV entries pinned. Did you check 'kv_last_accessed' histogram?
olivia: yes — mass of items with last_accessed ~30m ago; they should age out but TTLs are disabled for that workload.
nina: can we reproduce with a targeted replay? If it's longctx-driven perhaps prefix caching is holding references.
rachel: also check tenant quota config — T-309 has custom quota 0.35 (35%) on that node set, which is high. maybe noisy neighbor on same pool.
olivia: good call — node labels show T-402 (heavy batch infer) colocated on same GPU pool. SRE-bot reported high KV allocations earlier.
sre-bot: alert: kv-residency-high for tenant=T-309 node=gpu-pool-7 threshold=150k pages
ed: Suggestion: try 'quota_burst=0.1' and enable 'aggressive_reclaim' experiment on a canary host. Also add tenant-level sampling to track per-epoch reuse.
marc: for debug, can we flip to 'evict_oldest' instead of 'score-based' on the canary? command:
```
redwoodctl infra set-kv-policy --node gpu-pool-7 --policy evict_oldest --tenant T-309
```
devin: be careful — evict_oldest may regress latency for active longctxs. prefer simulated run: `./kv-sim --trace longctx_T309 --policy evict_oldest`
olivia: running sim now, will post results. ETA 20m.
... later ...
olivia: sim shows evict_oldest reduced resident pages by ~40% but increased p99 token latency by 120ms on longctx traces.
nina: okay tradeoff. Maybe hybrid: prefer evict_oldest for pages with reuse_score<0.02, otherwise keep.
rachel: could we implement 'reuse_score' fast-path in runtime? That's a small heuristics change.
ed: I'll PR a micro-change to eviction scorer to apply threshold-based fast-path. I'll include perf test.
marc: also let's add tenant-level hard cap as a safety: `tenant_kv_hard_cap = min(config_quota, 0.5*node_memory)` to avoid runaway.
olivia: created issue https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2321 linking pprof and sim results.
sre-bot: note: scheduled canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC on gpu-pool-7.
rachel: thx everyone. if olivia's sim looks stable we can canary with ed's PR + hard cap + sampling.
olivia: thanks — I'll update infra ticket after canary. :thumbsup:
